newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds cautious before FOMC, crucial support nearby.
newsitem.headline: Bunds cautious before FOMC, crucial support nearby.

text.p: German Bunds and futures started Tuesday's session nevously after the long weekend, with analysts saying the market is unlikely to make much progress ahead of a key U.S. monetary policy-setting meeting later.

With U.S. economists split 50/50 on whether the Federal Reserve will move to tighten interest rates at the FOMC, some traders said the risk was for a Treasury-led debt market sell-off if the Fed were to move.
"The market is pretty weak here this morning," said one Frankfurt-based trader. "We're all just waiting to see what happens to the U.S. later on."
By 0733 GMT, the DTB June future was trading 30 basis points lower at 101.54, struggling to hold above key technical support around 101.50.
The contract dipped briefly below this support in early trade but quickly pulled back.
The 10-year cash benchmark Bund was at 101.36, down 10 basis points, yielding 5.81 percent, with the 10-year spread to Treasuries steady at around 101 basis points.
Traders said some of the early slippage was down to the German market playing catch-up with weakness in LIFFE Bund futures on Monday when the DTB exchange was closed.
As well as the threat of an FOMC U.S. rate rise, analysts said Bunds would remain jittery about domestic plans to plug the deficit hole with a supplementary budget measures.
Until clear, credible plans were released, they said German debt would be under pressure amid the uncertainty.
April M3 money supply data is also expected to be released early this week, with analysts forecasting that growth will slow to 7.8 percent versus 1996 from 8.3 percent in March.
But with the Bundesbank very unlikely to be prompted into any rate easing by the M3 slowdown, analysts said the data would have limited market impact.
